articleTitle: Hybrid Beamforming Architecture and Wide Bandwidth True-Time Delay for Future High Speed Communications 5G and Beyond 5G Beamforming System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Multi Antenna systems such as beamforming and MIMO are anticipated to play a key role in 5G and beyond 5G communications. The Phased Array Antennas(PAAs) with phase shifter is the dominant method to achieve beamforming up to now. However the operation bandwidth of PAAs is limited to narrow(~200MHz) due to beam-squint problem. In beyond 5G, hundreds of Gbps data rate are required so the traditional PAAs based beamforming will face technical difficulties in the future. In this paper we proposed new beamforming architecture and an analog True-time delay(TTD) circuit which covers 4.8 GHz bandwidth. The architecture is a combination of phase shifters and TTDs. The analog TTD is composed of all-pass filter based cascade delay cells. The experimentally demonstrated TTD can support 590 psec total-delays with 40 psec resolution which covers more than 1024 number of array in mm-wave 5G system. The measured delay variance is within 4.09 % over the whole operating bandwidth. As a result the proposed scheme is a good candidate for large array and wide width beamforming system.

articleTitle: A 1.25Gbps Programmable FPGA I/O Buffer with Multi-Standard Support
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a field programmable gate array (FPGA) I/O buffer developed to support 1.25 gigabits-per-second differential source-synchronous standards is presented. The I/O buffer provides the compatibility of 38 high-speed I/O standards, features wide supply voltage range, programmable drive strength and controlled impedance driver. To enhance the performance and drive capacity of low voltage standards, an auxiliary supply is introduced into the I/O buffer. The proposed I/O buffer has been fabricated and integrated in an SRAM-based FPGA with commercial 65nm CMOS technology.

articleTitle: A 0.5-5.6 GHz Inductorless Wideband LNA with Local Active Feedback
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband low noise amplifier (LNA) with local active feedback is proposed. The proposed LNA exploits a differential common-source stage with current-reuse technique to reduce the power consumption. A source follower is utilized as an active feedback path and the feedback signal is taken preceding the cascode transistor to broaden the bandwidth and improve the linearity. Implemented in a 130-nm SOI CMOS technology, the proposed LNA achieves simulated 21.1 dB voltage gain with a 3-dB bandwidth of 0.5-5.6 GHz without using any inductors. The minimum NF is 3.63 dB while the maximum IIP3 is −4.86 dBm. The power consumption is 15.2 mW under a supply voltage of 1.5 V.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Power Bandgap Voltage Reference for IoT RFID Communication
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The reference voltage is a core part of RFID tags, its performance directly determines the whole chip's life and performance. The temperature coefficient is one of the important performances of the reference voltage source and the high-order temperature compensation is an effective method to reduce the temperature coefficient of the reference source. A low temperature coefficient bandgap reference is designed based on the standard 65nm CMOS process, and the low-supply voltage operation with bandgap reference circuit with current mode structure. The designed CMOS bandgap voltage reference is in the range of -20°C to 100°C with temperature coefficient of 9.6 ppm/°C and provides a good Power Supply Rejection Ratio(PSRR) of 79dB in the low frequency. The results of simulation show that the design improve the performance of the bandgap reference voltage source effectively.

articleTitle: Research on Improved Virtual Synchronous Generator Based on Differential Compensation Link
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Aiming at the contradiction between the dynamic and steady-state characteristics of conventional output power control for virtual synchronous generator (VSG) based on first-order link virtual inertia, a VSG control strategy based on differential compensation and bandpass damping power feedback is proposed. The control strategy adds a differential compensation link and a band-pass damping power feedback link to the forward channel of the conventional VSG control structure, thereby ensuring the steady-state control accuracy of the output power, accelerating the dynamic power response speed, increasing the system damping, and effectively reducing The energy impact of the dynamic process of the energy storage unit. The simulation verified the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: A Precision Voltage Reference Circuit with Trimming for 16-Bit SAR ADC in 55nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A low temperature coefficient voltage reference circuit for a 16-bit successive-approximation-register analog-digital-converter (SAR ADC) is presented in this paper. Including high-order compensation technique, logarithmic compensation technique and power supply rejection ratio (PSRR) enhancement technique are applied to this design. In addition, in order to pursue better temperature coefficient and output voltage accuracy, three kinds of trimming methods have applied to this design. This proposed design was implemented in a standard 55 nm CMOS process, the simulation results have shown temperature coefficient(TC) as low as 3.3 ppm/°C over a temperature range of 165°C (- 40°C to 125°C), the line regulation at room temperature is only 3.5 ppm/V, the circuit performs a PSRR property of 120dB@lkHz.

articleTitle: Metal-Semiconductor-Metal (MSM) Varactor Based on AlGaN/GaN Heterostructure with Cutoff Frequency of 914.5GHz for Terahertz Frequency Multiplication
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The design, fabrication and characteristics of planar metal-semiconductor-metal (MSM) two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) varactors based on AlGaN/GaN high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) for terahertz multiplication are presented. The gate length of ~450nm and the gate distance of 1μm are processed by using electron beam lithography (EBL). The DC characteristic shows a very low current leakage of ~7.3 ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-11</sup> A/mm, which is advantageous to the power consumption of terahertz multiplier. S-parameters are measured to obtain the high-frequency performance. The series resistance (R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>)of ~ 41.26 Ω, and the capacitance (C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>) of ~4.22 fF are abstracted respectively by matching the equivalent circuit at zero bias voltage. The cutoff frequency is of ~ 914.5 GHz. The capacitance switching ration (C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>/C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</sub>) is ≥ 2.4, and the figure of merit (FOM) is above 2.2 THz.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer System with Long Wired Repeater
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The magnetic resonant coupling wireless power transfer system (MRC- WPT) is a key technology for charging batteries anytime and anywhere. In this paper, we propose a novel power transfer system for enabling long distance transmission. It consists of a repeater connecting two coils by wiring, transmitter, and receiver. The system can not only send power far but enables free movement of the position of the receiver. Experiments demonstrate that the system can transmit power at further distances while maintaining high power transfer efficiency (PTE). Even with a length of 10 m between the two coils of the repeater, the system is as efficient as it is at a distance less than 1 m.

articleTitle: Optimization of Full-Chip Power Distribution Networks in 3D ICs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to minimize resources of power distribution networks (PDNs) in a three-dimensional integrated circuit (3D IC) under the given design constraints. We first present modeling of PDNs with RC reduction. Next, we describe the optimization of PDN parameters using a multi-objective optimization algorithm. The decoupling capacitors, on-chip power/ground grids, and power/ground through-silicon vias (TSVs), which have a great influence on the voltage drop (IR drop) and on the chip area increase, are optimized. The experimental results demonstrate that the new proposed method is effective for designing PDNs in 3D ICs.

articleTitle: A Novel LC VCO with High Output Power and Low Phase Noise Using Differential Active Inductor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a novel LC voltage-controlled-oscillator (VCO) based on active inductor (AI). Taking advantage of equivalent RLC model of the AI, a novel tunable differential AI (DAI) is designed and used to act as the LC tank of the VCO. First, a tunable DAI with cascode-structure and current-mirror feedback networks is designed to achieve high quality factor (\pmbQ) and high equivalent parallel resistance (Rp). Then, the DAI is used to replace LC in VCO to realize good comprehensive performance of VCO such as low phase noise, low power consumption and high output power. Based on TSMC 0.18μm RF CMOS process, the novel VCO is verified by Agilent's Advanced Design System (ADS). The results show that under the supply voltage of 1.8V, the output power reaches up to -4.2 dBm, a frequency tuning range is in 1.126-2.713 GHz, and the phase noise at 1-MHz offset is -117.2 dBc/Hz. A power of only 13.6 mW is consumed.

articleTitle: A Novel PWM/PFM Control Technique for Transient Improvement and High Efficiency Over a Wide Load Range in Buck DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a novel pulse width modulation (PWM) and pulse frequency modulation (PFM) control technique to improve the transient response when the converter transition from PFM mode to PWM mode and improve efficiency over a wide load range. The proposed PWM/PFM control technique used multiplexers combines PWM modulator and PFM modulator together to simplify the circuit. There are two parallel paths to realize the transition from PFM mode to PWM mode for improving transient response. The first path dominates mode transition when the load current changes from light to 120mA-260mA, the second path dominates mode transition when the load current changes from light to 260mA-1A. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed PWM/PFM control technique can realize auto-mode transition between PWM mode and PFM mode. The undershoot voltage is 75.8mV and recovery time is 3.3μs when the load current changes instantaneously from 10mA to 1A. Meanwhile, above 80% conversion efficiency can be reached over a load current range of 10mA-1A.

articleTitle: Parallel Integrated State Variable Filter Circuit Design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a parallel state variable filter circuit is designed. The integrated operational amplifier is used as the amplifying circuit. The state variable method is used to solve the differential equation to realize the high-pass, low-pass and band-pass band-stop filtering functions of parallel filtering. Through the Cadence software simulation, the state variable filter high-pass circuit cut-off frequency is 32.9KHz, the low-pass circuit cut-off frequency is 1.7KHz, the band-pass circuit center frequency is 7.0KHz, the band-stop circuit center frequency is 7.0KHz. The quality factor of the filter is 0.2, which is significantly better than other designs under the same conditions. Finally, the circuit layout is drawn using Cadence software. In this paper, the circuit simulation, layout drawing and verification are carried out with Virtuso, Spectre and Caliber software integrated in the Cadence system.

articleTitle: An 8-bit 400-MS/s Asynchronous SAR ADC with Single-ended/Differential Configurable Input Mode
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents an 8-bit 400-MS/s asynchronous single-channel successive approximation register analog-to-digital converter (SAR ADC) with single-ended/differential configurable input mode. In the sampling and holding circuit., three bootstrap switch circuits are combined with a level shift module., so the configuration of the single-ended/differential input mode could be realized. A improved split capacitor array technique is applied to decrease the digital-to-analog converter (DAC) settling time. Moreover., the design optimizes the logic delay of the SAR controller., resulting in a better match between the internal clock signal and the DAC settling time. The proposed ADC is simulated in SMIC 65-nm 1.2-V CMOS technology. In differential mode, it consumes 2.26-mW and achieves a signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) of 49.55-dB., translating into a figure-of-merit (FOM) of 23-fJ/conversion-step. In single-ended mode, it consumes 1.94-mW and achieves a SNDR of 46.87-dB., translating into a FOM of 26-fJ/conversion-step.

Author Keywords: the configuration of the single-ended/differential input mode

articleTitle: All-Digital Delta-Sigma TDC with Differential Multipath Pre-Skewed Gated Delay Line Time Integrator
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents an all-digital 1st-order 1-bit delta-sigma time-to-digital converter ( ΔΣ TDC) with a differential multipath pre-skewed bi-directional gated delay line (BDGDL) time integrator. Differential time integration is obtained by performing simultaneous left-shift and right-shift operations of the BDGDL. Pre-skewing is used to lower the per-stage delay and skew error of BDGDL. The time integrator features low power consumption accredited to the use of only one BDGDL to perform differential time integration, rapid time integration, full compatibility with technology, and built-in digitization. The TDC was designed in an IBM 130 nm 1.2 V CMOS technology and analyzed using Spectre from Cadence Design Systems with BSIM4 device models. A sinusoidal time input of 333 ps amplitude and 244 kHz frequency is digitized by the TDC. Simulation results show the TDC provides 39.7 dB SNDR, 6.5 ENOB, and 3.7 ps time resolution over frequency range from flicker noise corner frequency 32 kHz to 3rd harmonic frequency 732 kHz while consuming 407 μW. The FOM of the TDC is 3.2 Pj/step, outperforming that of reported TDCs alike.

Author Keywords: delta-sigma time-to-digital converter TDC) hi-directional gated delay line (BDGDL) pre-skewed BDGDL

articleTitle: Analysis of Transient Stability with SSSC and UPFC with Multi-Band PSS in Two Area Multi-Machine System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Power system stability plays a vital role in the growth of large interconnected power systems. Today's power system continues to expand in an exponential way due to an extensively automated need of both domestic and industrial needs. The ever-growing demand of power system network has resulted in rotor angle oscillations and voltage instability. In this paper, Static synchronous series compensator (SSSC) and Unified power flow controller (UPFC) are employed to analyze the transient stability of the power network with multi-band power system stabilizer (MB-PSS). The two area four machine power network has been considered to illustrate the performance of UPFC and SSSC in coordination with MB-PSS. To investigate the achievements of the designed system simulation has been carried out in MATLAB/Simulink software. The simulation results show that UPFC with MB-PSS controller gives a better improvement in transient stability compared with SSSC coordinated with MB-PSS.

articleTitle: Accurate Fault Location Method and Verification Test Analysis of High-Voltage Cable Hybrid Lines
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the wide application of high-voltage cable-overhead hybrid line, it is difficult to determine the fault zone and accurately locate the fault point based on the line fault location method with uniform parameters. For this reason, this paper proposes a two-terminal fault exact positioning method based on wavelet theory. The power frequency transient signals of fault currents in the head and the end of high-voltage cable are collected to determine the polarity of the fault to locate the fault section. The fault current can be accurately located by collecting the double-ended traveling wave signal of the fault current. A 110 kV high voltage cable state simulation test platform was constructed to carry out fault simulation tests within and outside the high voltage cable line to verify the actual effect of the fault location method. The experimental verification shows that the two-terminal fault exact positioning method based on wavelet theory can accurately determine whether the fault point is located interval or outside the interval of high-voltage cable line, and achieve the precise positioning of fault points in the high-voltage cable interval. This method will effectively reduce the time of fault finding, and is of great significance for fast recovery of power supply.

articleTitle: A CMOS Laser Driver with Configurable Optical Power for Time-of-Flight 3D-Sensing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A fast-pulse, configurable output optical power and high-pulse frequency integrated CMOS laser driver for 3D sensing is presented in this paper. The architecture of the proposed laser driver uses a DC-coupled structure, while risetime improvement is achieved by adding a resistor in parallel with the VCSEL. The proposed integrated laser driver is implemented in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.18\mu \text{m}$</tex> CMOS process with a 3.3V power supply. The measurement results show that the laser driver can deliver 0.20-0.92W configurable optical power to free space at a 100MHz pulse repetition rate.

articleTitle: Research on Very Fast Transient Overvoltage During Switching of Disconnector in 550kV GIS
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper establishes a circuit-simulation model about 550kV gas insulated switchgear (GIS) of Hongping pumped storage power station by using Electro-Magnetic Transient Program (EMTP). Then, the very fast transient overvoltage (VFTO) is calculated when the transformer, the bus line and the outgoing line are switched. As to the calculation results, the influence of VFTO on transformer as well as the influence of cable on VFTO are analyzed. Analysis shows that VFTO amplitude at transformer port is small, but it may excite significant internal resonance voltage under high-frequency oscillation which may harm the turn insulation of power transformer. Besides, long cable connecting the ground part and underground part of GIS accelerates the attenuation of the transient progress. Finally, the case in which the most serious VFTO of transformer port appears is chosen as a model to research the VFTO's suppressing measure. The research reveals that building a 3-meter-long overhead line between GIS bushing and transformer can effectively keep the wave front steepness below the restriction level. The wave front steepness of VFTO decreases by 30.2% from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1631}\ \mathbf{kV}/\mu\mathrm{s}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1138}\mathbf{kV}/\mu \mathbf{s}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Thermal Management for Future Wrist Wearable Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Wearable devices are evolving at a rapid pace. Many researchers are studying wireless power transfer technologies. Functions beyond current smartphone capabilities must be realized in wearable devices that are smaller than smartphones. Heat due to power consumption causes both circuit malfunctions and low-temperature burns to users. In this paper, we propose thermal management methods for future wrist wearable devices with higher performance. The methods include the reconstruction of a 3D IC, the heatspreader within a device, and the built-in heatspreader and surface fin heatsink of a belt. Our experiments with a FEM-based 3D thermal solver demonstrate that the new proposed methods can achieve 44.9% reduction in the gradient coefficients of °C /W.

articleTitle: Rapid Production of Customised Electronic Systems Via Multifunctional Additive Manufacturing Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Multifunctional additive manufacturing technologies can facilitate the rapid development and direct production of full-functional electronic devices by coupling the capabilities of additive manufacturing processes with other types of manufacturing techniques. In addition, these methods present evident advantages for improving the development speed and complexity of mass customized electronic products. In this work, we propose a multifunctional additive manufacturing solution that integrates dual-material fused deposition modeling 3D printing and selective electroless plating. Nickel alloy film can be selectively plated on 3D printed free-form plastic structures. With four-point probe investigation, EDS anlysis and SEM imaging, it was identified that the resistivity of plated film can be regulated by controlling the electroless plating parameters including reaction temperature and pH value. A minimal resistivity of nickel alloy film was approximate 8.4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup>Ω·cm, when the electroless plating was conducted at 50°C and pH 8.5. A 555 timer circuit with blinking LED was fabricated in both 2D and 3D manner as a demonstrator to prove the feasibility of this technology in practical industry applications.

articleTitle: Usage and Application of Power Quality Monitor on Harmonic Measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the large number of PV access in the medium and low voltage distribution network, the power quality problem of distribution network is becoming increasingly prominent. Therefore, it is necessary to test the power quality of distribution network with PV access and observe its power quality periodically. Based on this, this paper introduces the current commonly used power quality analyzer, and mainly describes the application steps and points for attention of HIOKIPW3198 power quality analyzer. Finally, this paper takes Shanghai Xinsheng semiconductor photovoltaic power generation system for an example, using HIOKIPW3198 power quality analyzer to test power quality on its workshop and 1# transformer low voltage side. Through the test and analysis, it is found that the voltage imbalance and frequency deviation of the company are within the allowable range, but there are slight voltage harmonic problems and serious current harmonic problems. The suggestion is that some measures should be taken to solve the problem. Otherwise, the power supply safety and quality of the company will be affected.

articleTitle: Research on Risk Assessment in Distribution Network with PV Generations
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Based on the fact that the traditional power system is suffering more influence after the access of PV generations, this paper focuses on the risk assessment in distribution network system with PV generations. It takes two situations into account, PV in different nodes and different PV capacities. Firstly simulates PV output which can reflect the PV characteristics, and then calculates power flow to get the nodes voltage amplitude and branch flow. Finally accesses the risk in distribution network with PV generations about the two situations mentioned above according to the risk indicators. Taking the IEEE 34 case and an actual distribution network as examples, the risk assessment of the distribution network with PV is carried out. The results show that the closer the PV position is to the end of the line, the higher the voltage will be. In addition, when PV is connected, the possibility of voltage limitation is larger than that of branch flow.

articleTitle: Design of a Multiple Channel Capacitance Measurement Integrated Circuit for Electronic Skin Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Capacitance measure is a technique for applications such as capacitance tomography and capacitive sensor readout. This paper presents a multiple channel capacitance measurement IC which is based on a switched-capacitor design in 0.18um process. It can be used on electronic-skin or other array-type sensors system. It contains of capacitance voltage conversion units and a single-slope ADC. It uses multiple channels at the same time to compensate the disadvantage on speed. Test result shows that the dynamic range can reach 45.1dB, and the conversion rate is about 5us/row in this paper.

articleTitle: Application of the Genetic Algorithm in MOSFET Modeling and Parameter Extraction
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, the genetic algorithm is introduced into parameter optimization for MOSFET small-signal model parameter extraction for up to 60 GHz millimeter-wave operations. Initial parameters of the model are extracted by curve fitting and direct parameter extraction method in saturation region approximately, and then fourteen independent parameters of the equivalent circuit model are optimized together. The real and imaginary part of S-parameter are set as the fitting targets simultaneously in this study. With the more convenient genetic algorithm, the model with the optimized parameters gives a better fitting accuracy than the initial parameters without optimization.

articleTitle: Design of Reliability Test Device for SPI Interface ReRAM Memory
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper designs a reliability test device for Fujitsu 4Mbit SPI interface ReRAM memory. The device uses FPGA as the lower computer controller to realize the basic data writing and reading operation of the SPI interface ReRAM memory. The upper computer software supports the programmable instrument control, the data writing and reading function test of the ReRAM memory, the SEU detection under the continuous reading operation, the continuous writing and reading function test of the specified address. It can be used for the reliability test of SEE, data retention and endurance of ReRAM memory. In the SEE sensitivity test, it is found that the device is prone to SEFI under heavy ion irradiation. After stopping the beam and restarting the system, the data of the ReRAM storage unit has not changed, which proves that the SEU of the data storage unit array has not occurred.

articleTitle: A 1.8V Output RF Energy Harvester at Input Available Power of −20 dBm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a RF energy harvester (RFEH) operating at a frequency of 900 MHz in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.18-1\mu\text{m}$</tex> CMOS technology. It mainly consists of an RF rectifier, a low dropout voltage regulator (LDO), and a self-starting circuit. A level-l hybrid forward and backward compensation technique is employed for the RF rectifier to lower the equivalent threshold voltage of MOS transistors, which can optimize the sensitivity of the RFEH and the power conversion efficiency (PCE). The LDO is adopted at the output of the RFEH to reduce the output voltage ripple remarkably. The self-starting circuit makes the RFEH perform the energy harvesting without the assistance of external supply. Simulation results show that the RFEH can produce an output voltage of 1.8V and achieve a PCE of 41.2% at an input available power of −20dBm.

articleTitle: Calibration Mechanism for Input/Output Termination Resistance in 28nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a method of receiver and transmitter input/output resistance calibration in UMC 28nm CMOS process. Designed and verified in Cadence IC615, the actual calibration resistance of the simulation (approximately 200Ω, which is four times the impedance of the transmission line) with high robustness under all PVT conditions, and the maximum deviation is 0.85%. The proposed calibration mechanism can be applied to high-speed interface circuits such as LVDS, LVPECL, CML, etc.

articleTitle: Design of Super Capacitor Charging Management Integrated Circuit for Energy Harvesting Based on Reconfigurable Photovoltaic Cells Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a super capacitor charging management integrated circuit (IC) based on reconfigurable photovoltaic cells array is proposed. This IC is based on a novel maximum power point tracking (MPPT) method that arranges photovoltaic (PV) cells into different combination networks in order to optimize the charging efficiency dynamically. With the reconfigurable PV array, various voltage outputs of PV cells charge the super capacitor without inductor based switching regulator. The MPPT circuit is designed according to the I-V characteristics and P-V characteristics of the PV cells. Depending on the charging stage of the super capacitor, different series/parallel combination networks of the PV cells are selected to make the PV cells work in the vicinity of the maximum output power to achieve a higher charging efficiency. Charging current of a single PV ranges from 10μA to 100μA, the charging efficiency from a small PV cells array to IF-5V super capacitor can reach more than 80%, up to 94%.

articleTitle: Electrical Power System Stability Enhancement by Using an Optimal Fuzzy PID Controller for TCSC with Dual TCRs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In recent years, there has been an incredible increase in power demand but power generation and transmission expansion is insufficient because of environmental restrictions and limited resources. Therefore, it has led to transmission systems to be operated nearer to their stability and thermal limits which may further encounter additional problems with interconnections or weak ac links while retaining the emphasis on quality of power to be delivered. In order to desire the security requirement, stability, controllability and maximum system loadability, Thyristor based (FACTS) controller, thyristor Controlled Series Capacitor (TCSC) is equipped in a transmission line. In this paper, an optimal fuzzy PID controller is designed for TCSC with dual TCRs. The controller of a TCSC is designed on the basis of system impedance. An optimal fuzzy PID controller is obtained through using fuzzy logic (FL) and genetic algorithm (GA). To investigate the achievements of optimal fuzzy PID controller, simulation has been conducted in MATLAB/Simulink software. The accuracy of the designed controller well checked on three machine-nine bus system. The simulations results showed that the optimal fuzzy PID controller can generate an improved dynamic response.

articleTitle: An Arithmetic Unit and Multiplying Accumulation Unit of a Custom Floating Point Data Format
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a floating point multiplication and accumulation operator based on FPGA is designed for neural network calculation, and a custom 32 bit floating-point data format is used to change the amount of computation by changing the overall structure of the data, and the performance of the operator is optimized. Finally, the simulation results in FPGA are given to verify the correctness of the design. The design saves the resources by comparing the floating point operation with the common algorithm of 32 bit floating-point data of the IEEE standard.

articleTitle: Image Preprocessing of Iris Recognition
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to propose the methods for image preprocessing of iris recognition including image enhancement and boundary detection. Iris recognition has been widely considered as one of the most dependable identification method. However, the iris systems are still not widespread due to many factors, for example, the production cost, the processing time and the recognition rate. The problems of production cost and the processing time will be resolved with the development of integrate circuit technology. The problem of recognition rate mentioned here is not about the iris itself, but the acquisition of the effective image of the iris. The quality of the iris image has become the key point of the current iris system. The preprocessing of iris recognition involves hardware and software design of the system and in this paper both of the designs are discussed.

articleTitle: The Characterization of Superconducting Tungsten Thin Films Deposited by DC Magnetron Sputtering
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, we studied on the nanometer tungsten (W) thin films deposited onto Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/Si substrates by DC magnetron sputtering. The morphologies, crystal structures and components of W thin films with different thicknesses were investigated. The four-terminal electrodes structure was prepared by microfabrication technology and the electrical and superconducting properties of W thin films were measured. All results show that the W thin films are mainly composed of β-W under our experimental growth conditions. The superconducting transition temperature (Tc) of the W thin film with different thickness fluctuates from 1.15K to 1.65K.

articleTitle: An Active Inductor Based Quadrature Voltage-Controlled Oscillator in $\mathbf{0.13}\mu\mathbf{m}$ CMOS
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The design and measurement of a voltage controlled oscillator with quadrature outputs using a CMOS active inductor is presented. The coarse tuning of the quadrature VCO (QVCO) is accomplished through bias current tuning and varactors are added for fine tuning. The oscillator facilitates two working states. When supplied with 1.2 V supply voltage, the tuning range is 1-2 GHz and the phase noise (PN) varies from -71 dBc to -110 dBc at a 1 MHz offset from the carrier frequency. When the QVCO is supplied with 1 V supply voltage, the frequency tuning range is 0.7-1.5 GHz and the measured phase noise is from -71 dBc to -102 dBc at a 1 MHz offset. The output power varies less than 2 dB along all working conditions. The QVCO occupies an area less than 0.015 mm2. Except the output buffer, it consumes 2.5-2.7 mA from 1 V supply and 6.4-7 mA from 1.2 V supply.

articleTitle: Research and Design of Class D Amplifier at 1 MHz
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper is mainly for the study of current mode Class-D(CMCD) power amplifier at 1MHz operating frequency. The article mainly focuses on the influence of the driving circuit of the power MOSFET on the Class-D amplifier at high frequency, the parameter calculation in the power amplifier circuit and the parameters of the output transformer. The calculations are discussed in three aspects. In addition, the article discusses the Class-D materials used in the circuit. The article realizes the development of a current-type Class-D amplifier based on the efficiency value of nearly 80% at the operating frequency of 1MHz, and it builds a specific circuit for physical design and verification.

articleTitle: Error Compensation Methods for Laser-Displacement-Sensors Surface Modeling
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Laser displacement sensors (LDSs) have been widely used in surface modeling for their pinpoint accuracy. To match the high accuracy of LDSs, the influence of machinery vibration must be compensated. In this letter, we built a mathematical model of the relative position between LDSs and objects. Based on the model, the Direct Compensation Method and the Curve Fitting Compensation Method were introduced to separate vibration components from original data for both part-known and completely unknown surfaces. A key and an inner face of a barrel were chosen for the verifications. Both methods were found compensating vibrations well.

articleTitle: Novel Design of SOI SiGe HBTs with High Johnson's Figure-of-Merit
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A novel design of SOI SiGe HBTs with a buried n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> thin layer and p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> doping layer is proposed to improve the product of cutoff frequency and breakdown voltage, which is a vital Johnson's figure of merit (J-FOM) of the device. In this design, the n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> thin layer is used to increase the cutoff frequency and the p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> doping layer is adopted to maintain a high breakdown voltage. Furthermore, the thickness of n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> thin layer is also studied to improve the J-FOM. As a result, for the novel SOI SiGe HBT, the J-FOM is increased from 351.5GHz-V to 482.3GHz-V, when compared with that of the traditional device. This design effectively develops the application of SOI SiGe HBTs in microwave power.

articleTitle: The Design of Low Temperature Coefficient Band-Gap Reference
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Sometimes, the high-resolution A/D or D/A converter all need a high precision reference, the voltage of reference will determine the precision of the conversion result. In whole system, it always requires that the conversion result should be in a specified range in a wide temperature range. In order to release the variation range of conversion result, it requires that the temperature coefficient of reference should be very small. In this paper, it introduces one higher order compensated band-gap reference, it uses the current Ib from the existing structure to compensate the higher-order voltage of VBE. In this way, the temperature coefficient of this Band-Gap Reference will be less than 1ppm/°C in theory.

articleTitle: A Novel Hardware Trojan Protection Technology Based on Logic Encryption
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the rapid development of integrated circuits and microsystems, the security of this IC industry is getting more and more attention [1]. Therefore, there may be malicious circuit insertion at various stages, resulting in functional failure, performance degradation. In order to prevent the circuit from being plugged into the hardware Trojan, there are now some hardware Trojan protection technologies, including logic encryption, BISA technology and so on. Among them, logic encryption technology makes it difficult for hardware Trojan attackers to insert Trojans for rare nodes by obfuscating the circuits. This paper proposes a novel hardware Trojan protection technology based on logic encryption, which not only defenses against this attack technique of Hamming distance, but also proposes a fake rare node to confuse the circuit.

articleTitle: Architectures and Design Techniques of Digital Time Interpolators
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper provides an in-depth review of the principle, architecture, and design techniques of digital time interpolators. An assessment of the advantages and drawbacks of analog time interpolators are presented first. It is followed with a comprehensive examination of reported digital time interpolators including gated inverter time interpolators, harmonic-rejection time interpolators, voltage-division time interpolators, and pipelined time interpolators. The design considerations of digital time interpolators including input signaling, output signaling, input-output isolation, and shoot-through are studied in detailed. The performance of recently reported digital time interpolators is compared. Finally, a 5-bit digital-to-time converter with 2-bit time interpolation is designed in a TSMC 65 nm 1.0 V CMOS technology and analyzed using Spectre from Cadence Design Systems with BSIM4.4 device models. Simulation results are presented.

Author Keywords: Time-based signal processing digital time interpolator digital-to-time converters

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Routing: A Methodology for PPA Tradeoff in Network-On-Chips
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposes a routing algorithm design methodology based on real network traffic analysis. The method aims at large-scaled network on chip in which load differs among different areas or routing nodes. By applying different routing algorithms on different nodes, the area and/or power consumption can be saved only at the cost of minor performance loss. Experimental results show that by replacing routing nodes using NoP routing algorithm with nodes using XY routing algorithm, up to 10% of routing nodes can be simplified into much less power/area costing nodes, saving at least 2 % of area overhead, only at the cost of 5% of performance loss.

articleTitle: Locking Range Property of Single-phase Injected Divide-by-3 Injection-Locked Frequency Divider at High-Injection Power
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This letter studies a wide-locking range divide-by-3 CMOS LC-tank injection locked frequency divider (ILFD) subjected to high injection power larger than 0 dBm and describes the operation principle of the ILFD. The ILFD circuit is realized with a double cross-coupled CMOS LC-tank oscillator with one injection MOS. The self-oscillating VCO is injection-locked by third-harmonic input to obtain the division factor of three. Measurement and simulation shows the locking range saturates at high injection power and then starts decreasing as injection power further increases.

Author Keywords: single-phase injected divide-by-3 injection-locked frequency divider

articleTitle: Feedback Linearization Control Scheme for DFIG with DC-Based Converter System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposes feedback linearization control (FBLC) scheme for the strongly-coupled DFIG with DC-based converter system which is applied in the VSC-HVDC power transmission system. This converter system consists of a stator side converter (SSC) and a rotor side converter (RSC). The stator and rotor of DFIG are connected to the DC-bus through SSC and RSC respectively. Since the voltages of rotor and stator are controlled by RSC and SSC simultaneously, the DC-based converter system is strongly coupled. Therefore, FBLC is adopted to control the strongly coupled system and linearize the system with full decoupling. FBLC controllers for RSC and SSC are designed to guarantee that DFIG operates at maximum power point (MPP) and stator flux keeps stable and the rotor current could track its reference closely and quickly in the stator flux-oriented frame. At last, the simulation is carried out. The results validate the feasibility of the proposed control scheme even if in the case of ramp-change wind speed.

articleTitle: Radio Frequency System-On-Chip Design for Digital Receiver
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The design, processing and testing of a single RF system on chip (SoC) system is completed on the basis of wideband radio frequency receiving circuit, low power and highspeed high precision analog to digital converter(ADC), digital down converter(DDC), central processing unit (CPU) and other complex functional circuits. The research of a radio frequency(RF) SoC integration technology with wideband radio frequency signal receiving, analog digital conversion, digital signal processing and control is carried out, which lays a technical foundation for the realization of the digital radio frequency receiver SoC.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Ampacity Rating of 500kV Overhead Transmission Lines in Zhejiang Province
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Due to the limitation of power transmission capability, the renewable energy generation may be curtailed in summer season. Since the corridors are too crowd to build new transmission lines in Zhejiang province, it is an urgent demand to enhance the ampacity of existing transmission lines. This work applied the probabilistic ampacity rating method to 20 circuits of 500kV transmission lines in Zhejiang province. The weather conditions in the transmission lines corridors are first analyzed and typical meteorological year (TMY) is generated. Secondly, the hourly ampacity distributions of the transmission line are calculated. Finally, the ampacity of transmission lines are determined at different acceptable risk levels. Significant ampacity enhancement was achieved by the application of probabilistic ampacity rating method.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Insulation in Compact Switchgear Based on ANSYS Simulation and Partial Discharge Test
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: An optimal design and layout of the insulation structure in the compact switchgear is proposed to improve its insulation effect. Firstly, electric field simulation and partial discharge test for the shielding effect of busbar through-wall bushing and contact box shielding are carried out. Then, test analysis of the condensation characteristics of the switchgear and electric field simulation of the influence of condensation on the electric field distribution of the insulator are carried out. Finally, the insulation components of the switchgear cable room are optimized. The insulation performance is verified by electric field simulation and partial discharge test.

articleTitle: A 14-bit 500MS/s and 1GS/s Configurable Pipelined ADC with Background Calibration
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 14-bit 500-MS/s and 1-GS/s configurable pipelined Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) is implemented in 28 nm CMOS. The ADC leverages dither and correlation-based background digital calibration techniques to correct the interstage gain and settling errors. A dithering technique is employed to inject a large dither signal to randomize residual non-linearity in the pipelined ADC. In order to speed up the correlation-based calibration, a variable-step-size LMS algorithm is used to extract the error coefficients. An optional interleaved mode is provided, where the two ADCs on a chip are time-interleaved to realize a single 14-bit 1 GS/s ADC. After calibration, the ADC achieves a 61.64 dB SNDR and 71.83 dB SFDR at 1 GS/s sample rate. The chip occupies 6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> area and consumes 1.4 W at 2.0/1.0 V supplies.

articleTitle: A Low Energy Consumption Passive RF Activation Circuit with Stable Output
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In order to solve the energy consumption problem of active RFID tag and prolong the battery life, a passive RF activation circuit without source power, which composed of diodes and capacitors, is studied in this paper. The circuit collects and converts RF energy to DC power. Therefore, it does not need power supply and can efficiently decrease the power consumption. The electromagnetic co-simulation simulation results show that the circuit can generate about 1.5V DC stable output when the antenna absorbs -20dBm RF power (Standard RFID power signal is -10~-50dBm, so average figure is chosen here). It is very suitable for application in electronic documents and device management with their normal operation voltage always 1-2V.

articleTitle: Modeling of Monolithic Spiral Inductors with Patterned Ground Shield for Si-Based RF IC's
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: An improved single-π equivalent circuit model with patterned ground shield is presented in this paper. The monolithic spiral inductor uses metal 1 and metal 2 as a ground shield which forms a good isolation between substrate and passive device at the high frequency. To accurate model for spiral inductor under the high frequency, a parallel L-R network is adopted to represent the high-order effects. A C-L-R network to model the ground loop in the lower metal strips. Within the wide bandwidth, the modeling and parameter extraction methods have been validated by the excellent agreement between the circuit model and EM-simulation up to 40GHz.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Bandpass Filter Design and Verification with De-embedding Technology in SiP Solutions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, the design, trade-offs, chip-level simulation and verification of a miniaturized radio frequency (RF) filter with low insertion loss and high rejection have been demonstrated. The proposed architecture of the bandpass filter (BPF) consists of a multi-order cascaded LC network and ground coupled sections which introduce resonant zeros and poles in the passband. The BPFs with two topologies are presented in this work, followed by performance comparison and investigation. Implemented with a high resistivity silicon integrated passive device (IPD) process, the BPF features a compact die area of 0.75 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 0.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> respectively, including seal ring at each side of the chip. The IPD filter design is validated with a probing setup by locating the IPD chips on a test board with wire bonding package. In order to evaluate the package degradation on the overall performance, the bonding wires and test fixtures on the test board have been respectively modeled and de-embedded, together with an on-board calibration during the probe measurement.

articleTitle: Realization of System Verification Platform of IoT Smart Node Chip
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the development of large scale integrated circuits, the functions of the IoT chips have been increasingly perfect. The verification work has become one of the most important aspects. On the one hand, an efficient verification platform can ensure the correctness of the design. On the other hand, it can shorten the chip design cycle and reduce the design cost. In this paper, based on a transmission protocol of the IoT node, we propose a verification method which combines simulation verification and FPGA-based prototype verification. We also constructed a system verification platform for the IoT smart node chip combining two kinds of verification above. We have simulated and verificatied the related functions of the node chip using this platform successfully. It has a great reference value.

articleTitle: A Wideband Tunable Voltage Controlled Oscillator Supporting Non-harmonically-Related Multiple Frequency Bands for Future 5G Applications Using $\mathbf{0.13}-\mu \mathbf{m}$ SiGe BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A wideband tunable Voltage Controlled Oscillator (VCO) that covers the two 5G frequency bands dedicated for future 5G communication, is presented in this paper. The two distinct frequency bands are selected by switching ON and OFF the fixed capacitance of the resonator. The designed VCO is integrated with a novel distributed biased wideband varactor circuit to achieve the desired range at the targeted bands. The oscillator can be continuously tuned in a wide bandwidth from 27 GHz to 39.5 GHz., thereby covering the two 5G bands (28 GHz and 38 GHz) with a stand-alone LC oscillator. The simulated phase noise at 28 GHz and 38 GHz are recorded as -93 dBc/Hz and -90 dBc/Hz., respectively. The total power consumption is 9.7mW from a 1.2 V supply.

articleTitle: Failure Analysis on the Abnormal Leakage of the Transistors at Lower Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Failure location and mechanism analysis of a type of transistors failure are presented in this work. The failure phenomenon of abnormal leakage appeared in the collector terminal at low temperatures test. A series of methods including residual gas analysis (RGA), decapping internal inspection, isolation exclusion test and verification test are adopted to analyze the cause of the failure. Based on scanning electron microscope and energy spectrum analyzer examination, the abnormal leakage between the collector and the base terminal is caused by the multiple factors coupling effect. The effect factors include micro cracks in the passivation layer, the internal moisture and the trace of the movable ion. The formation of micro cracks in the passivation layer lies on abnormal passivation process of the chip. It is beneficial to guide the improvement of process control in foundries. Analysis and test method in this failure case could be useful to the similar failure analysis in the future.

articleTitle: A 10 GS/s, 3-Bit ADC with Novel Decoder in SiGe BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a design of 10-GS/s, 3-bit analog-to-digital converter in a 0.13 μm SiGe BiCMOS technology for optical communication application. This fully differential flash ADC includes a wide-bandwidth track-and-hold amplifier, a high-resolution comparator array and a novel differential decoder. By using our novel differential decoder, this ADC design achieves better than 2.8 effective bits for lower input frequencies and 2.5 effective bits for 1 GHz input frequency at a sampling rate of 10 GS/s. This ADC consumes 1.6 W with a 10 GS/s clock rate, while operating from -5/-3.3 V power supplies and its core area is only occupies 1×1.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: OMAPL138 Based Image Acquisition and Display System Development
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: An OMAPL38 based high sensitive CMOS image acquisition and display system has been developed. This system is designed for iris recognition which requires high speed and high sensitive raw images. The image size of the system is 752×480 (10bit) and the experimental results indicate that the readout speed exceeds 60fps with the peak quantum efficiency over 50%. This system opens new possibilities for the real-time biometric matching of eye images. The hardware and software details are described in this paper.

articleTitle: A Three-level SVPWM Control Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The three-level Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation (SVPWM) principle is shown. A novel space vector modulation algorithm which use positive or negative small vectors as first active vector is presented. The judging rules of the small sectors and the out voltage vector sequence are presented as well as the producing of the signals for SVPWM. Also, the dwelling time of each out voltage is computed. The analysis of other sectors is realized by transforming the sectors. The validity of the proposed method is demonstrated by the simulation results.

articleTitle: One Method to Fit Biexponential Curve by Using Fourier Transform
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Many physical phenomena can be described by biexponential curve. To study the physical phenomena, there is a need to obtain their mathematical expressions. Generally, the expressions are acquired based on the fitting of experimental data, and the general method to fit exponential curve is nonlinear least squares (NLLS). In the NLLS method, it is crucial to choose good enough starting values for the parameters, otherwise, the fitting might fail to converge. In this paper, one new method is proposed to solve the problem, which utilizes the Fourier transform to transform the non-linear exponential fitting model into a linear one. It makes the estimation of the parameters independent of the initial values and easy to converge. The fitting result shows that the proposed method can be used to fit the curve expressed by difference of double exponentials.

articleTitle: The Design of High Linear Bootstrapped S/H Switch
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Sometimes, the input-port of A/D converter always needs a S/H switch. In Sample state, the S/H switch should always be opening, now voltages between input-port and output-port in S/H switch are always the same. In Hold state, the S/H switch should always be closing, now the voltage of output-port in S/H switch will keep a fixed value, and it will not be changed with the voltage of input-port in S/H switch. For A/D converter, the conversion linearity is the most important parameter. For getting the best performance of conversion linearity, it is very important to design a high linear S/H switch. In sample stage, the voltage of output-port in S/H switch should be always changed with the voltage of input-port at any time. It is very easy to S/H switch design under the normal condition. Next for getting the higher linear performance in A/D converter, the fixed value in Hold state should be keeping linear performance of input voltage at the most, it is very hard in high resolution A/D converter. Through this paper's design, it makes the distortion leading by Sample switch become linear distortion. So it can get a high performance S/H bootstrapped switch, which can apply to 16-bit or much higher resolution ADC.

articleTitle: A High-Temperature Model of MOSFET Characteristics in $0.13-\mu \text{m}$ Bulk CMOS
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: There is an increasing demand for reliable high-temperature electronics implemented in low-cost bulk CMOS technologies. In this paper, first, a detailed study of high-temperature impairments and reliability issues is presented. An analytical model for high-temperature operation of MOSFET devices in 0.13-μm bulk CMOS process is then presented. The proposed large-signal model includes temperature effect on the leakage current, carrier mobility and threshold voltage. The small-signal model includes temperature effect on the transconductance and output impedance. A prototype has been made in 0.13-μm bulk CMOS. The I-V transfer characteristics have been measured at different temperatures from 25°C to 200°C. The experimental results are compared with the simulation results from the developed model. The simulation results demonstrate a very good agreement with the experimental data. The EDA tools models provided by the foundry do not generally guarantee model correctness at high temperatures. Therefore, the foundry models of the 0.13-μm CMOS process have been simulated to verify the model reliability at high temperatures. The EDA tools results are overall in close agreement with the measured data, which shows the reliability of the transistor model for the 0.13-μm technology at high-temperature.

articleTitle: A 108-dB SNDR 2–1 MASH $\Delta\Sigma$ Modulator with First-Stage Multibit for Audio Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a 108dB SNDR 2-1 MASH switched-capacitor ΔΣ modulator in standard 0.18μm CMOS technology. The Silva-Steensgaard structure and 4-level quantizer are adopted in the first stage of a 2-1 multistage noise shaping (MASH) topology, which ensure modulator's stability, sufficient noise shaping and power efficiency. Meanwhile, modulator coefficients are optimized for low power consumption. Also, the 4-level quantizer reduces the inherent noise leakage in the MASH ΔΣ modulator. The data weighted average (DWA) technology in high power efficiency is implemented to address the nonlinearities caused by mismatch among the feedback DAC unit elements. Chopper stabilization (CHS) and bootstrapped switch are implemented to respectively reduce 1/f noise and harmonic distortion. Simulation results show that for an oversampling ratio (OSR) of 100, this modulator achieves a peak SNR of 108.88dB, a peak SNDR of 108.02dB and a Schreier FoM of 173.78dB based on SNDR with a 22.05kHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Novel Phase-Locked Loop-Enabled Power Estimator for Single-Phase Power Electronic Converters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposes an active and reactive power estimator incorporating a novel phase-locked loop (PLL) for single-phase power electronic applications. The proposed estimator includes: 1) a new PLL algorithm preceded by a smooth variable structure filter (SVSF) to synchronize grid voltage signal and minimize the noise influence of the grid voltage signal and 2) a fast upper-triangular and diagonal recursive least square (FUDRLS)-based active and reactive power estimation algorithm using instantaneous power signal and estimated phase angle from the proposed PLL. The proposed method provides more accurate and faster active and reactive power estimation than conventional recursive least square (RLS)-based and discrete Fourier transform (DFT)-based methods. Moreover, the proposed estimator is relatively insensitive to noise since the SVSF is inherently robust to noise and to modeling uncertainties. Due to its low computational complexity and numerical stability, the proposed method is suitable for the real-time embedded system to estimate active and reactive power and for an alternative PLL method for control applications of the grid-connected converters.

articleTitle: ACE Speech Processing Strategy and Feature Analysis in CI Device
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In clinical application, cochlear implant (CI) is an important medical device to help many persons with severe deafness to obtain auditory sensation. Speech processing strategy is the most important part in CI device, which extracts signal feature of the desired voice and then modulates the original signal to adapt to signal transmission and electrode stimulation. The advanced combined encoder (ACE) method is one of the most famous speech processing strategies applied in the present CI device. In this paper, we research the algorithm structure of ACE strategy and analyze the signal feature after signal modulation, aiming to improve the speech recognition for further algorithm research.

articleTitle: Research and Design of Extended Permutation Module for RISC Processor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Based on the butterfly network, extended permutation module is designed in this paper. Effectively reducing the hardware area by using the same circuit structure to implement arbitrary permutation and multi-width shift operation. At the same time, the transposition instruction is designed for RISC processor, so it has better practical value. In the case of area and delay only increasing by 25.6% and 13.1%, the unit implements a variety of width rotation shift, logical shift and arithmetic shift, and permutation operation of width extensible, which has high application value in cryptography, digital image processing and other fields.

articleTitle: A Ring Ocillator Based Reliability Monitor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Due to the technology nodes further scale, variabilities continue to be a challenge for IC design. The variability is mainly classified as IR-drop, temperature change and aging. We mainly discussed the first two parts in this paper. Overheating can damage the chip permanently and excessive IR-Drop can greatly affect voltage sensitive digital blocks. In order to avoid these damages and make better adaptation, we need to differentiate these variabilities. In this paper, a 32nm ring oscillator based temperature sensor with IR-Drop monitor was presented. Different from traditional sensors, the proposed sensor can monitor IR-Drop in-field which avoid its effect on temperature measurement. The IR-Drop monitor is sensitive to variations larger than 100mV. Meanwhile, the temperature sensor block has a wide temperature measurement range. The sensor's temperature measurement period could be close to 10us,which helps to establish real-time thermal management. With its help, we can improve chip reliability. All these parts can be easily integrated into a chip due to its all-digital cells. The sensor occupies less than 0.0 1mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> area and achieves a resolution of 0.5°C.

articleTitle: Influence of Cable Terminal Floating Potential Defect on Electric Field
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: To research the influence of floating potential defect on electric field distribution, an electric field simulation software applying the finite element method was adopted to establish a simulation model for computing the electric field distribution around the cable terminal. The influence of different lengths of defects on the maximum electric field are analyzed. Oscillation wave partial discharge test system was established. The results show that the maximum electric field intensity of the defect area increases with the increasing of the length of the metal plate first, then decreases, and finally increases. The maximum electric field intensity increases linearly with the changing of the cable core voltage, and the maximum electric field value exceeds the design value. Oscillatory wave test results show that floating potential defect can easily make electric field aberrant and lead to significant PD phenomenon, verifying that the electric field simulation result is correct.

articleTitle: A Novel One-Step Calibration Method for On-Chip Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A novel one-step calibration method with no iteration and high trimming accuracy for on-chip oscillator is proposed. The concept is to count oscillator cycles within a specified reference period of time, and take the count value as the trimming code of oscillator to achieve the targeted frequency. To demonstrate the effectiveness of this method, an on-chip RC relaxation oscillator with 8-bits trimming signal has been designed, analyzed and verified with a 0.5um CMOS technology. Simulation results show that the oscillator achieves a low frequency variation of ±0.8% over ±45% process variation of resistor and capacitor after one-step calibration.

articleTitle: Online Measurement Method for Parameters of Transmission Line Based on PMU
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The traditional off-line measurement method for parameters of transmission line must deploy the equipment and personnel at both of the line. The earth loop has effect on the measurement result, especially the winter soil is frozen. To this end, the measurement method based on PMU is proposed. Using the synchronized phasor measurement, the method can eliminate the effects of the earth loop and measure online. In this paper, the effectiveness of the method is verified by the simulation example and actual measurement data. The sample precision of all the measured electric quantities are determined by sensitivity analysis. The results show that the existing PMU can meet the engineering accuracy requirements.

articleTitle: Study on Statistical Evaluation of Supply Reliability for Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The reliability of power supply for users is an actual reflection of power supply enterprises in sustained power supply for users. The current statistical methods of power supply reliability for users adopted currently are mainly based on medium-voltage distribution transformer statistics, which is hard to truly reflect the genuine reliability level for users. This paper has put forward reliability statistical evaluation methods, carried out statistical analysis and calculation to the power supply reliability of medium-voltage users and low-voltage users, and analyzed the impact of different statistical methods for the power supply reliability index. Finally, the feasibility of the calculating modes has been verified by choosing some areas of Shanghai as an example of application, and suggestions on improvement of power supply reliability statistical evaluation for low-voltage users implemented by power supply enterprise have been expounded.

articleTitle: A High Dynamic Range Broadband SoC Design for Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a very high dynamic range SoC for radar applications, which including a broadband high linearity RF transceiver, a 16bit 125Msps high resolution ADC, a 14bit 1Gsps high speed DDS and the DDC. The IM3 cancellation technique was used to acquire very high linearity of the RF transceiver. By using the digital calibration technique to improve the resolution of the ADC. The chip using the 0.18um BiCMOS process to realize high integration and good performances. The test results show that, the gain flatness is less than 1dB of the RF frequency range from 200MHz to 4GHz, the noise figure of the RX is less than 5.3dB, the OPldB and OlP3 of the receiver is larger than 20dBm and 40dBm, respectively. The output power of transmitter is larger than 15dBm. The SFDR of ADC is 89dBc at 125Msps with the digital calibration. The SFDR of DDS is 95dBc at 120Msps. The power consumption is 2W of RX mode and 2.3W of TX mode, respectively.

articleTitle: Power Characteristics for the Dual Channel 4H-SiC Metal Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The current and breakdown characteristics of a dual channel 4H-SiC metal semiconductor field effect transistor (4H-SiC MESFET) are studied by using simulation tool ISE-TCAD. The simulated results show that current density of the dual channel structure is much higher than that of the conventional structure at the same gate bias. The breakdown happened in the gate terminal close to the drain and the breakdown voltage of the dual channel 4H-SiC MESFET is 120V, 50% higher than that of the conventional 4H-SiC MESFET because there is a more dispersive electric field distribution. So, the dual channel 4H-SiC MESFET has better power performance, when compared with the conventional structure.

articleTitle: A 1-V 90.3-dB DR 100-kHz BW 4th-Order Single Bit Sigma-Delta Modulator in 40-nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 1-V 4th-order discrete-time single bit sigma-delta modulator over a signal bandwidth of 100 kHz is presented in this paper. The feed forward topology is selected to reduce the voltage swings of the integrators. In addition, a novel two-stage inverter-based amplifier is proposed to improve the DC gain in low voltage environment. To save power consumption, a pure dynamic comparator is employed. Designed and implemented in 40-nm CMOS technology, the modulator achieves 88.5 dB peak SNDR (signal-to-noise and distortion ratio) and 90.3 dB DR (dynamic range). The core area of the chip is 0.133 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the total power consumption is 1 mW.

articleTitle: Repeated Strike Process Modeling of Very Fast Transient Overvoltage Induced by Disconnector Switch Operation in 252kV GIS
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: It is a problem that the existing very fast transient overvoltage (VFTO) repeated strike simulation model doesn't take strike characteristics of the contact gap into account and the arc resistance model can not fully reflect the dynamic changes of the arc. Firstly, a 252 kV GIS experiment platform is established to obtain strike characteristics by closing/opening disconnector. Secondly, considering peak value of current, length of contact gap and air pressure, combined with the arc extinction law of special fast transient overcurrent (VFTC), a double exponential high frequency arc resistance model is proposed. Finally, based on the discharge voltage curve and arc resistance model, the whole-process VFTO simulation model of 252kV GIS is established. Variable step method is used to alternate calculations of the power-frequency steady process and high-frequency transient process to obtain an efficient and accurate simulation.

articleTitle: Implementation of Multipath Transformer in CMOS Voltage-Controlled Oscillator CMOS VCO Using Multi-Path Transformer
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A complementary oscillator was implemented in the TSMC 0.18 μm 1P6M CMOS process, and it uses spiral multipath transformer to increase the quality factor of passive transformer. The multi-path transformer consists of a 3-path inductor internal to a single-path inductor used as the secondary inductor. The oscillator uses the Accumulation-mode MOS varactors for frequency tuning. The VCO uses no dynamic bias to lower the power consumption in steady state and the core current and power consumption of the oscillator are 4.05 mA and 4.457 m W, respectively at the de drain-source bias of 1.1 V. The oscillator can generate differential signals in the frequency range of 3.3-3.62 GHz. The die area of the oscillator is 1.148×0.987 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Response Analysis of a 2D MEMS Electromagnetically Driven Micro-Mirror
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: As a MEMS actuator device, the 2D micro-mirror works in two resonant modes to realize biaxial deflection in light detection and ranging (LiDAR) system. By Changing the exit angle of the incident laser, the three-dimensional information of a space object can be received. This paper researches on the response problem of one kind of 2D electromagnetically driven micro-mirror by numerical analysis and finite element analysis method. The aim of response analysis is to obtain the angle matching of biaxial deflection under a certain proportional driving force. The dynamic model of the mirror was established firstly. Then, a numerical method called Newmark-β method was used to design optimized structure and simulate time domain response of the mirror.
